absent: Numeric values and widths of extension magics, header sizes, terminator size, and maximum frame size.
Full C layouts, padding, and offsets of native and compat frames and context records.
Size computation and offset assignment for the native user layout.
Internals of preserve and restore helpers for each extension and of user access state handling.
Validation rules for user registers, fault address and code, and alternate stack restore.
Locking, preemption, and concurrency rules around signal setup and return.
Vector trampoline and compat signal page contents and restorer selection details beyond flags.
First part of the user frame parser before the routed range.

findings.text: Native signal return is entered through a zero argument system call that treats the current stack pointer as the address of the frame to restore.
Compat realtime frame setup is globally visible and builds a 32 bit realtime frame then arranges handler entry.
Compat non realtime frame setup is globally visible and builds a 32 bit legacy frame then arranges handler entry.
Compat restart setup is globally visible and records the compat restart number in the 32 bit syscall register.

Mode and guarded stack extension records are accepted only when the matching feature is present and only once per frame, with repeats rejected and the user address and length remembered for later restore.

At most one extra descriptor is accepted per parse. It must cover its own header, its payload address and length are fetched with fault propagation, a zeroed generic terminator must fit and follow inside the original bounds, and parsing then restarts once over the extra region.

Extra payload acceptance requires sixteen byte alignment of both address and length, exact adjacency of the payload to the post terminator position, containment within a bounded maximum frame budget, and accessibility of the whole extra span.

Every record must at least cover a generic header and fit within the remaining bytes. The cursor advances by the claimed size and any short, overrunning, unknown, or duplicated record fails the whole parse as invalid.

Signal return restoration follows an ordered discipline of mask update on successful copy, general plus stack plus program counter plus status restoration with restart suppression, floating point save and flush, user register validation, frame parse, then feature gated extension restores with scalar state mandatory and scalable state preferred when present.

Guarded stack signal return is a no operation build variant in one configuration. In the enabled configuration it is a no operation without support or without shadow stack enablement, else it orders prior stack operations, checks a capability word at the current pointer against an expected value, clears the slot, and advances by one word.

Signal return requires a sixteen byte aligned stack pointer and an accessible fixed size frame. Restoration, guarded stack validation, and alternate stack restoration must all succeed, with the success value taken from the first argument register.

Native frame creation writes unwind linkage, general state, fault address, and mask first, then preserves each extension only while error free at its precomputed offset when its feature is present, finishing with an extra descriptor plus terminators and a final zero terminator.

Extra descriptor setup reserves a descriptor plus headers, publishes the address immediately after them as payload start with length extending to the rounded total size, marks the descriptor with its magic and size, and zeroes both terminators.

Native frame placement initializes a layout, computes sizes, selects the signal stack top, reserves a sixteen byte aligned unwind record then the frame itself with sixteen byte rounding, and requires writability of the whole span.

Guarded stack handler entry is a no operation without support or enablement. Otherwise it stores the trampoline address and a signal capability below the current pointer and decrements the pointer by two words, propagating store faults.

Handler entry chooses an application restorer when flagged else a vector trampoline, performs fallible guarded stack entry first, then infallibly switches argument, stack, frame, link, and program counter to handler context with signal number and optional info and context pointers.

Handler entry brands the branch type for indirect call semantics when that extension exists, always clears tag check override, and when matrix extension exists disables streaming and matrix storage while clearing the related thread register.

Native realtime orchestration flushes floating point, allocates the frame with allocation failure mapped to nonzero, saves access state, clears flags and link, saves alternate stack, builds the frame, conditionally copies signal info, then either commits handler access state or restores the saved one.
Restart setup dispatches on task compatibility to write the appropriate restart number into the architecture specific system call register.

Signal delivery notifies restartable sequences, then selects compat realtime, compat legacy, or native builders based on task mode and info flag, combines a user register sanity check into the status, and forwards single step state to completion handling.
Compat frame allocation selects the signal stack top, subtracts the requested size with eight byte alignment, and yields null when the span is not writable.

Compat handler entry derives Thumb mode from the handler low bit, synthesizes status with instruction set and execution state adjusted and transient execution state cleared, selects restorer or vector slot indexed by mode and info flag, then switches argument, stack, link, program counter, and status.

Compat frame content maps native general registers to 32 bit context slots with status converted to compat form, publishes trap and fault and mask fields with both legacy and full mask copies, preserves floating point when present, and terminates with a zero marker.
Compat mask publication splits the first native mask word into low and high halves for the two compat words.

Compat floating point preservation flushes hardware state, writes magic and size, copies the lower sixteen double precision halves from packed vectors, synthesizes control status from status and control masks, and writes a synthetic exception word with zeroed companion fields.

Compat realtime setup copies signal info and clears flags and link while the legacy variant uses a fixed flag pattern without info. Both allocate with null mapped to nonzero, save alternate stack, build the shared frame, and configure return only when error free.
Parsed user contexts are collected as per extension user pointers plus lengths for scalar, scalable, matrix, thread, mode, guarded, and permission state, with absence represented as null.
Native layout carries a sigframe pointer, an unwind record pointer, per extension offsets for each preserved state plus extra and end, and a total size used for placement and bounds.
Compat auxiliary area appends a floating point frame followed by a single end magic word.
Native signal stack and extra payload require sixteen byte alignment with fifteen as misalignment mask. Compat frames require eight byte alignment.
General restoration covers thirty one registers. Guarded stack return advances one word while entry reserves two words.

Context discrimination uses named magics for extra, guarded, scalar, scalable, matrix, thread, mode, permission, and exception state plus zeroed generic terminators, a zero native flags value, and fixed compat flag and exception patterns.

Once handler registers including stack are updated, failure must not occur because a nested fault handler would corrupt the outer return state. Guarded entry is therefore completed before the switch and later steps are infallible.

Any signal return validation failure including misaligned stack, inaccessible frame, restore error, guarded validation error, or alternate stack error converges to a fault notification at the stack pointer with zero return rather than propagating errno.
Guarded return clears the validated capability word before advancing, preventing replay of the same token.
Repeated extra descriptors are rejected and parsing state is reset to the extra region only once, preventing looping or repeated parsing.
